cf.title: Vacuum statistics
cf.authors: Andrei Lepikhov (lepikhov), Andrei Zubkov (zubkov), Alena Rybakina (a.rybakina)

verdict_reasoning: Patches 0001-0004 draw no surviving objection, and the thread shows demand for them. The hook and contrib module in 0005-0008 fail at level 1b. Two reviewers asked which vacuum settings the counters would tune, and message #151 defers the answer (demand-1). The material also does not say why the storage module must ship in contrib (already-exists-2), and it cites no field report (demand-2).

brief.title: Cumulative vacuum statistics per table, index and database
brief.problem: Vacuum work details (buffers, WAL, timing, dead and frozen tuples, pages) appear only in pg_stat_progress_vacuum while a vacuum runs, or once in the VACUUM VERBOSE or autovacuum log line. DBAs who tune autovacuum have no cumulative per-object view of vacuum workload over time.
brief.proposed_design: The current v47 series has two parts. Patches 0001-0004 add a few columns to existing pg_stat views and a per-index removed-tuples count to the VERBOSE log line. Patches 0005-0008 add a core hook that receives a report after each table and index vacuum, plus a contrib extension that stores the reports as custom cumulative statistics; 0009 tracks clearing of visibility map bits.
user_visible_surface: VACUUM VERBOSE and autovacuum log: per-index line gains "tuples: N removed".
pg_stat_all_indexes, pg_stat_all_tables, pg_stat_database: total_(auto)vacuum_time and total_(auto)vacuum_delay_time columns where not already present.
pg_stat_all_tables and pg_stat_database: vacuum_failsafe_count; pg_stat_database: vacuum_interrupt_count.
C API: set_report_vacuum_hook, plus geterrlevel() in elog.h and visibilitymap_clear_rel().
contrib ext_vacuum_statistics: pg_stats_vacuum_tables, pg_stats_vacuum_indexes and pg_stats_vacuum_database views, reset functions, and the vacuum_statistics.enabled GUC.
author_claims: Without the extension loaded, the core overhead is a small stack struct and a NULL check on the hook.
The heap report subtracts index buffer and WAL usage, so serial and parallel vacuum do not double-count.
The log-line data is printed once and lost, so it cannot serve as queryable cumulative statistics.
A dropped relation's entry is removed through object_access_hook, so OID reuse does not inherit old statistics.
Patches 0001-0004 are useful on their own, apart from the hook and extension.
brief.thread_state: Since 2024 the design moved from in-core views to an extension, back to core, then to the hook plus extension after Bharath and Amit argued most data exists in instrumentation and belongs in a module. Korotkov, Bharath, Karina and Vlada reviewed v42-v44; v47 has had no reply, and CFbot shows it needs a rebase.
unclear: The material does not say which vacuum settings these statistics would tune; the author promised that answer later.
Starting the server once without the module resets all cumulative statistics, built-in ones included; the material does not say whether reviewers accept this.
The material does not say whether 0009 (VM bit clearing) moves to its own thread, as Bharath asked.
The material does not show memory overhead for many tables, other than one README estimate of about 700 KB for 3000 objects.
Hook placement for table AMs other than heap is not described.

prior_attempts.title: Add last_vacuum_index_scans in pg_stat_all_tables
prior_attempts.quote: No other stats counter works that way; they are all additive.
prior_attempts.reason: Alvaro Herrera objected that the column keeps only the last vacuum's value, unlike other stats counters, which are all additive; he and Peter Geoghegan said a history of vacuum runs would be more useful. Fujii Masao asked whether one global counter in a pg_stat_vacuum view would be enough, and Alvaro later doubted the tuning value because autovacuum memory is capped at 1 GB. The author did not resolve these points, and the visible thread ends with a request for a rebased patch that got no reply before the entry was withdrawn.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P1 kept only the last vacuum's index-scan count in one column. This proposal keeps additive cumulative counters, which answers the recorded objection, and puts most detail in an extension.

objections.title: No vacuum setting is named that the extension statistics would tune
objections.failure_scenario: A DBA loads ext_vacuum_statistics and sees about 30 cumulative counters per table and index. No documented step leads from any counter to a change in autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit, maintenance_work_mem or another setting, so the DBA watches the numbers and makes no tuning decision. The project then maintains a core hook and a contrib module that does not change what users do.
objections.argument: Amit asked in message #105 how these statistics would be used to tune vacuum, and Bharath repeated the question in message #150. In message #151 the author defers the answer and says it will come later. The stated goal in message #1 is tuning, so the case for 0005-0008 depends on that missing answer.
objections.author_must_show: For three or four counters in 0005-0008, which vacuum setting does each one change, and what does a DBA see before and after the change?

critic.reasoning: Messages #118 and #151 give some interpretations, such as delay time pointing to cost-based settings. But the author states in #151 that the mapping from statistics to settings will come later, so the question from #105 and #150 is still open.

objections.title: Once the hook exists, the storage module need not be in contrib
objections.failure_scenario: The project commits ext_vacuum_statistics with its views, reset functions, GUC and custom stats kinds, and then owns fixes to its parallel accounting, OID-reuse handling and privileges. Messages #152-#158 show such bugs found late. If someone starts the server once without the module loaded, all cumulative statistics are reset, and users report that to the project.
objections.argument: Bharath (message #150) and Amit (message #105) proposed core hooks with an external module, along the lines of pg_stat_statements, and the author has kept the module on GitHub since message #114. With set_report_vacuum_hook in core, the proposal does not say the module needs contrib for catalog access, grammar or performance. Custom cumulative statistics work out of tree, so contrib placement mainly moves the maintenance burden onto the project.
objections.author_must_show: What does ext_vacuum_statistics gain from contrib that an out-of-tree module using set_report_vacuum_hook cannot have?

critic.reasoning: pg_stat_statements shows contrib placement has precedent, and a hook benefits from an in-tree user for testing. But the material does not say why the full storage module, not a small test module, must ship in contrib.

objections.title: Per-run vacuum data already exists in the log; demand for more is not shown
objections.failure_scenario: Operators who need per-table vacuum history today set log_autovacuum_min_duration = 0 and aggregate the log lines. 0001-0004 already add totals, delay times and failsafe counts to pg_stat views. The extra buffer, WAL and page breakdowns in 0005-0008 serve a group whose size the thread does not show.
objections.argument: Message #150 maps almost every metric in the series to a field the VACUUM VERBOSE or autovacuum log already prints. The author answers in message #151 that log data is lost to rotation and needs a parser. That is an inconvenience with a working remedy. The interest in the thread comes from reviewers and patch authors (messages #9, #68). No user report from -general or -bugs is cited, and the thread does not show production numbers.
objections.author_must_show: Which production cases, outside this thread, could not be diagnosed from the autovacuum log line plus the 0001-0004 columns, and what did those operators need instead?

critic.reasoning: Developers from several companies called the statistics useful (messages #9, #68, #108), which lowers confidence in this objection. Still, the thread cites no field report, and the log line covers most metrics except the per-index WAL and buffer breakdown.

other_surviving.title: In-core columns and extension columns use different accounting rules
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A monitoring query adds pg_stat_all_tables.total_vacuum_time to pg_stat_all_indexes.total_vacuum_time for a table and its indexes, and does the same with wal_bytes from pg_stats_vacuum_tables and pg_stats_vacuum_indexes. The time total counts index work twice. The WAL total does not, so the derived per-table cost is wrong in one view and right in the other.
other_surviving.argument: 0002 keeps table total_vacuum_time covering the whole heap_vacuum_rel() run, index time included. The new index columns duplicate part of it, and pg_stat_database adds index time only once. 0007 and 0008 subtract index usage from the heap report so that sums do not double count. The two parts of one series then use opposite conventions for vacuum work that sit side by side.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which rule, table including or excluding its indexes, should all vacuum counters follow, and where is it documented for both the pg_stat_* columns and the extension views?

critic.reasoning: The 0002 text says table and database time include index processing, while 0007 and 0008 subtract index usage from the heap report. The existing total_vacuum_time semantics cannot change, but the series does not state one rule for both sets of counters.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Extension view and column names depart from cumulative statistics conventions
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A user who knows pg_stat_all_tables and pg_stats looks for pg_stat_vacuum_tables and does not find it, because the views are named pg_stats_vacuum_*, a prefix Postgres uses for planner statistics. Tools that join on schemaname and datname must alias schema and dbname. Reset functions named vacuum_statistics_reset and extvac_reset_entry do not match pg_stat_reset_* or pg_stat_statements_reset.
other_surviving.argument: Message #68 asked for "schemaname" for consistency, and message #74 agreed, but the v47 documentation for pg_stats_vacuum_tables still lists schema and dbname. Earlier in-core versions used pg_stat_vacuum_tables (message #146). The extension then changed to the pg_stats_ prefix without giving a reason. Names in a contrib module are hard to change once released.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Why do the views use the pg_stats_ prefix and schema/dbname columns rather than pg_stat_, schemaname and datname as existing cumulative statistics views do?

critic.reasoning: The v47 documentation lists schema and dbname columns and the pg_stats_vacuum_* names, although message #74 agreed to schemaname. The thread gives no reason for the change from the pg_stat_ prefix used through message #146.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Starting once without the module discards all built-in cumulative statistics
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A DBA tries ext_vacuum_statistics, then removes it from shared_preload_libraries and restarts. The server treats pg_stat/pgstat.stat as corrupted and resets every statistics kind, so n_dead_tup and n_ins_since_vacuum go to zero. Autovacuum then delays vacuums of bloated tables, and the DBA finds out when bloat or wraparound warnings appear.
other_surviving.argument: Message #154 states this outcome, and the 0005 documentation only warns about it and advises keeping the module loaded with vacuum_statistics.enabled = off. A contrib module that leaves state on disk which core cannot read without it means removing the module costs more than its own data. Autovacuum scheduling depends on the lost counters. This comes from the custom stats framework, but shipping it in contrib makes the case common, and the thread does not show reviewers accepting it.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Can the stats file reader skip entries of an unregistered custom kind, or can the module drop its entries cleanly, so that removing it keeps the built-in counters?

critic.reasoning: Message #154 and the 0005 documentation confirm the reset of all kinds, and autovacuum does schedule on the lost counters. The effect matches a crash-recovery reset and hits only clusters that loaded the module, but the thread shows no reviewer accepting it.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Index-usage subtraction in vacuum code is fragile and fails silently
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A later patch adds or reshapes an index-processing path in vacuumlazy.c or vacuumparallel.c and omits the sampling and accumulation calls. The heap report then absorbs index buffer and WAL usage, or loses it. Core tests still pass, and only users comparing extension numbers with VACUUM VERBOSE notice.
other_surviving.argument: The thread shows the same class of error several times: index stats missing under parallel vacuum (#66, #80), parallel index passes unsampled (#147), worker usage double-counted (#157), and deleted pages double-counted (#160). Each was found by a reviewer, not by a test in the vacuum code itself. The bookkeeping lives in hot vacuum code that many people change, while the only check lives in a contrib TAP test.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Which check in core, independent of the contrib module, fails when a new index-processing path skips the sampling calls?

critic.reasoning: Messages #66, #147, #157 and #160 each show an accounting error in this bookkeeping that a reviewer found. The new TAP test in 0008 covers the current paths, but nothing fails when a later index-processing path omits the sampling calls.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Report hook is shaped for heap and for this one extension
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A table AM author or a second monitoring extension wants per-vacuum reports. The hook fires from heap_vacuum_rel and the parallel vacuum code with heap-specific fields such as missed_dead_tuples and visibility map pages, so other AMs get nothing unless they copy the machinery. Each later change to the report struct also breaks extension ABI.
other_surviving.argument: Message #61 asked that the machinery work for any table AM, and the reply in #66 renamed terms, but the material does not say where non-heap AMs call the hook. The struct grew across patches 0005 to 0008 to match this extension's views. Exporting geterrlevel() and visibilitymap_clear_rel() widens the API for the same feature.
other_surviving.author_must_show: What contract does set_report_vacuum_hook give to table AMs other than heap, and which report fields are AM-neutral?

critic.reasoning: The material does not say where a table AM other than heap calls the hook, and message #61 asked for that. The geterrlevel() point belongs to 0004 and does not support this objection, but the AM contract question stands without it.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Tuning use of the statistics is still unstated after two years
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA loads ext_vacuum_statistics and sees cumulative wal_fpi, missed_dead_pages and delay times per table. No documented rule maps any column to a change in autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit, maintenance_work_mem or the scale factors. The core hook and the new pg_stat columns then have to be kept up to date in every vacuumlazy.c change, with no agreed user decision behind them.
refuted.argument: In [P1], the doubt about the tuning value of a vacuum counter was one of the points left open when it was withdrawn; that summary is a pointer only. Amit (message #105) and Bharath (message #150) asked which settings these statistics would tune. In message #151 the author answers that the answer will come later. A committer would likely ask for that answer before adding a permanent hook and new view columns.
refuted.author_must_show: For two or three of the new counters, which vacuum setting would a DBA change based on them, and what does that DBA do today without them?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-1, which makes the same point from messages #105, #150 and #151 without relying on [P1]. [P1] concerned a last-value column, so it must not be used as support.

refuted.title: Starting once without the module resets all built-in cumulative statistics
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA removes ext_vacuum_statistics from shared_preload_libraries, or brings up a new cluster from a copied data directory without the module. At startup the server treats pgstat.stat as corrupted and drops every kind, including n_dead_tup and n_mod_since_analyze in pg_stat_all_tables. Autovacuum loses the counters it schedules on, and the DBA finds out only when tables stop being vacuumed on time.
refuted.argument: Message #154 and the 0005 documentation both state this behaviour, and the documented fix is to keep the module loaded with vacuum_statistics.enabled = off. A contrib module shipped with Postgres would then make an ordinary configuration change silently damage core state that autovacuum depends on. The proposal treats this as a property of custom stats kinds today and does not change that rule. The brief notes that no reviewer has said this is acceptable.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the stats file loader skip entries of an unregistered custom kind instead of discarding all kinds, and is that change part of this series?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same reset of built-in statistics and describes the effect on autovacuum more precisely.

refuted.title: User-settable vacuum_statistics.enabled lets sessions opt out of collection
refuted.failure_scenario: A non-superuser who owns a table runs `set vacuum_statistics.enabled = off` in a session and then runs manual VACUUM there. Those runs, including their WAL and buffer cost, never reach the cumulative views. The DBA relies on pg_stats_vacuum_database to judge vacuum load and only finds the gap when the numbers disagree with the logs or pg_stat_io.
refuted.argument: The README recipe uses a plain session `SET vacuum_statistics.enabled = off`, and the commit message for 0005 says the setting can be set per database. Together these suggest an ordinary user can change it. The core settings that control what cumulative statistics record (track_counts, track_io_timing, track_cost_delay_timing) are superuser-only, so that users cannot hide or skew what the DBA sees. The proposal does not give the GUC context or explain why this switch should differ from them.
refuted.author_must_show: What is the GucContext of vacuum_statistics.enabled, and if it is user-settable, why should it differ from track_counts and track_cost_delay_timing?

critic.reasoning: The scenario depends on the GUC being user-settable, and the material does not show its context. The README `SET` example and per-database setting are both possible with a superuser-only GUC, so this is a question for code review.

refuted.title: Running once without the module resets all built-in cumulative statistics
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA tries ext_vacuum_statistics, then removes it from shared_preload_libraries and restarts. The server treats pgstat.stat as corrupted and resets every kind, including n_dead_tup and n_mod_since_analyze, which drive autovacuum. Autovacuum scheduling is degraded until the counters rebuild, and the DBA finds out only after the restart.
refuted.argument: Message #154 and the 0005 documentation confirm this behaviour and offer a warning as the only answer. A warning is a weak fix for a contrib module that people will add and remove while evaluating it. Everyone's built-in statistics bear the cost, while only module users gain. A committer would likely ask for the loader, or this kind, to fail softly before contrib ships the first in-tree user of the trap.
refuted.author_must_show: Can the stats file loader skip entries of an unregistered custom kind, or can this module avoid persisting entries, so that removing it does not reset built-in statistics?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1. The item 4 framing also does not fit, because the reset affects only clusters that loaded the module.

refuted.title: Hook report repeats the counters the vacuum log line already prints
refuted.failure_scenario: A DBA who wants per-table vacuum history today sets log_autovacuum_min_duration = 0 and parses the log. With v47 the same numbers also come through set_report_vacuum_hook. A later patch that adds a counter to the VERBOSE line must also update the hook struct, and nothing fails if it does not.
refuted.argument: Message #150 maps 0002-0009 to existing output: tuples, pages, WAL, buffers, VM bits and timings in the VERBOSE and autovacuum log line, plus pg_statio_all_tables and total_vacuum_time in pg_stat_all_tables. Message #151 answers that log data is lost after printing. That shows the log path is less convenient, but it does not show the job cannot be done. The material still names no tuning decision that needs the queryable form, and the author has deferred that answer.
refuted.author_must_show: Which vacuum setting would a DBA change from these cumulative counters that cannot be decided today from the autovacuum log line plus pg_statio_all_tables?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of demand-2 for the log-line argument, and of demand-1 for the tuning question. The hook design itself came from the reviewers in messages #105 and #150, and a hook struct that lacks a new log counter is not a failure.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: The module writes custom kinds into the statistics file; a start without the module discards all cumulative statistics.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: 0002-0004 change system_views.sql and pg_proc.dat and bump catversion for new pg_stat columns.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: The series adds set_report_vacuum_hook and its report struct, geterrlevel() and visibilitymap_clear_rel().

touch_points.label: security / privileges
touch_points.reason: The module adds reset functions restricted to superusers by default, and views that show all relations.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: Sampling code in vacuumlazy.c and vacuumparallel.c, a core hook and a contrib module all need upkeep.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: Vacuum samples buffer and WAL usage around the heap run and each index pass, and pgstat entries gain fields.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)
touch_points.reason: Reviewers argued the detailed counters belong in a module, and that module could live out of tree.

questions: For three or four counters in 0005-0008, which vacuum setting does each one lead a DBA to change, and what does the DBA see before and after?
What does ext_vacuum_statistics gain from contrib that an out-of-tree module using set_report_vacuum_hook cannot have?
Which production cases could not be diagnosed from the autovacuum log line plus the 0001-0004 columns?
Can the statistics file reader skip entries of an unregistered custom kind, so that removing the module keeps the built-in counters?
Should all vacuum counters include or exclude index work in the table figure, and where is that rule documented for both sets of views?

committability.owner_note: It needs a committer who knows lazy vacuum, parallel vacuum and the cumulative statistics system. Reviewers commented on v42-v44, but v47 has no reply.
committability.liability: The owner signs for the hook and its report struct as extension API, the index-usage subtraction in vacuum code, and a contrib module with custom statistics kinds, for as long as they ship.
committability.author_follow_up: Strong sign: the authors have posted 47 versions since 2024 and keep moving the entry between CommitFests.

not_now.evidence_that_would_change_it: A worked mapping from a few of the 0005-0008 counters to specific autovacuum settings, plus field reports of cases that the autovacuum log line and the 0001-0004 columns could not diagnose.

priority.reason: The nine patches touch vacuumlazy.c, vacuumparallel.c, pgstat and a new contrib module, and the design changed direction several times. Patches 0001-0004 could go ahead as their own entry, while 0005-0008 wait for the tuning answer and the decision on contrib placement.

provisional_note: Five level 2 objections survived but were not evaluated because level 1b fails. Without the code, the GucContext of vacuum_statistics.enabled, hook chaining with object_access_hook, and the parallel accounting could not be checked.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add last_vacuum_index_scans in pg_stat_all_tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a last_vacuum_index_scans column to pg_stat_all_tables that shows how many index scans the last vacuum of each table needed. The author meant it as a signal for raising maintenance_work_mem or autovacuum_work_mem.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Alvaro Herrera objected that the column keeps only the last vacuum's value, unlike other stats counters, which are all additive; he and Peter Geoghegan said a history of vacuum runs would be more useful. Fujii Masao asked whether one global counter in a pg_stat_vacuum view would be enough, and Alvaro later doubted the tuning value because autovacuum memory is capped at 1 GB. The author did not resolve these points, and the visible thread ends with a request for a rebased patch that got no reply before the entry was withdrawn.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: No other stats counter works that way; they are all additive.

precedents_retrieved.title: SQL statements statistics counter view (pg_stat_sql)
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds a pg_stat_sql view that counts SQL statements executed on the instance by command tag, behind a new track_sql GUC, with a reset function. Later versions keep one row per command tag in a hash table, counted in exec_simple_query and exec_execute_message.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier returned the entry with feedback after months without activity, after Alvaro Herrera asked who would rebase it onto the new cmdtaglist.h enum tags. Andres Freund's 2017 review had left open questions: an extension might be the better place, tags should be enums in a fixed array, and counting belongs at the executor level. The author promised an array version, but the visible messages do not show one. A competing cmdstats patch by Mark Dilger also waited on benchmarks that Robert Haas requested.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch had no activity for months, so I am marking it as returned
with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Planning counters in pg_stat_statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add planning counters to pg_stat_statements: a count of how many times a statement was planned and the total planning time, recorded through a planner hook alongside the existing execution counters. The patch passed the planning time to the executor through a new PlannedStmt field and had the planner hook bump the existing nesting level counter.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Tom Lane objected to the design: pgss_ExecutorEnd cleared a field in the cached PlannedStmt, which he said amounted to modifying the plan cache. He also questioned whether the planner hook should change nested_level, and he said the approach assumed a near one-to-one relationship between planner and executor calls that does not hold for cases such as prepared statements. He proposed having the planner hook record planning time with its own pgss_store() call. The author found that this needs the query text in the planner, which would mean changing function signatures, and returned the patch with feedback because he did not have time to rework it during the commitfest.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
What we have here is pgss_ExecutorEnd stomping on the plan cache.
I do *not* find that acceptable.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add index scan progress to pg_stat_progress_vacuum
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds index vacuum progress to pg_stat_progress_vacuum, with counts of indexes to process and indexes processed, including indexes handled by parallel vacuum workers. Later versions keep worker progress in a hash table in the main shared memory segment, so the progress views can read it after a worker exits.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund and Robert Haas objected to the use of the main shared memory segment and to the locking it adds to progress reporting, which is meant to be low overhead. They asked that workers pass data to the leader through the parallel vacuum's dynamic shared memory, and that the leader report it with the existing progress fields; Masahiko Sawada agreed. Greg Stark returned the patch because of these design changes.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
That is, I am imagining that you would want to use DSM to propagate
data from workers back to the leader and then have the leader report
the data using the existing progress-reporting facilities.

precedents_retrieved.title: Flush SLRU counters in checkpointer process
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes the checkpointer report SLRU statistics during normal operation instead of only at server shutdown. After review it moved the WAL and SLRU stats reports into pgstat_report_checkpointer(), so they also run from CheckpointWriteDelay().
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch's new pg_stat_slru test failed on Windows CI in 031_recovery_conflict. The author traced this to a race on have_slrustats and said a more stable version would follow, but none was posted. The entry was then returned with feedback, which message #9 gives as a consensus to prioritise other patches because this one was not in good shape.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
There
are many patches to be reviewed and this one doesn't seem to be in the
best shape, so we have to prioritise.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add parallel counters to pg_stat_statements
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add counters to pg_stat_statements that record how many times a statement was planned with parallelism and how many times it ran with parallel workers. A later version instead counted how often a parallel plan ran without any parallel workers.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Julien Rouhaud said the counters cannot tell why a parallel plan ran without workers: the executor disabled parallel mode (!es_use_parallel_mode, as with the JDBC client) or no workers were free. He asked for separate counters for each case and for better column names. Nobody answered this review, and Michael Paquier marked the entry Returned with feedback after the thread had been idle for a few weeks.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Both situations are different and in my opinion require
different (and specialized) counters to properly handle them.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert "Avoid the creation of the free space map for small heap relations".
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert "Avoid the creation of the free space map for small heap relations".
Reverted commit(s): Improve code comments in b0eaa4c51b.; Avoid creation of the free space map for small heap relations, take 2.; During pg_upgrade, conditionally skip transfer of FSMs.; Add more tests for FSM.; Clear the local map when not used.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This feature was using a process local map to track the first few blocks
in the relation.  The map was reset each time we get the block with enough
freespace.  It was discussed that it would be better to track this map on
a per-relation basis in relcache and then invalidate the same whenever
vacuum frees up some space in the page or when FSM is created.  The new
design would be better both in terms of API design and performance.

List of commits reverted, in reverse chronological order:

06c8a5090e  Improve code comments in b0eaa4c51b.

precedents_retrieved.title: Split index and table statistics into different types of stats
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch splits the cumulative statistics kind PGSTAT_KIND_RELATION into PGSTAT_KIND_TABLE and a new PGSTAT_KIND_INDEX, with index-specific counting macros and SQL-callable functions. The goal is sensible field names for index stats and lower memory use, since index entries currently carry unused table counters.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stalled. Review comments from Andres Freund and Melanie Plageman were still open, and the author put the work on hold until the related "Generate pg_stat_get_xact*() functions with Macros" patch was done. After that patch was committed, no new version came; the CFM returned the entry because it no longer applied and tests failed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This patch no longer applies (with tests failing when it did), and the thread
has stalled.

precedents_retrieved.title: Extended statistics in EXPLAIN
precedents_retrieved.summary: Show in EXPLAIN (VERBOSE) which extended statistics objects the planner applied to a scan node and to which clauses, so users can see whether a statistics object affects an estimate. The PoC patch stores this information in lists added to the Plan and deparses the clauses the way index quals are deparsed.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The commitfest manager returned the entry because it had too little reviewer interest, and said the return was not a rejection. Earlier, Tom Lane objected that the feature exposes unstable planner internals, adds data and copying cost to every finished plan, and fails if a statistics object is dropped between planning and EXPLAIN. Robert Haas disputed this, and Tatsuro Yamada posted a rebase in January 2022, but no review followed before the entry was closed in August 2022.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: Rather than code changes, what this patch needs is more community interest.

roaster_notes.note: The only listed precedent close to this proposal, [P1], died on a non-additive counter, and this proposal fixes that. [P2] was closed for inactivity, which does not apply here. One objection is raised on the tuning question that [P1] and this thread both leave open.
Three objections apply from the standards and compatibility angle. The VERBOSE log line format change is left out, because Postgres does not promise a stable log format.

Other persistent state looks contained. pgstat file format and catversion bumps follow existing practice, cumulative stats are per node and not replicated as for built-in kinds, and drop and OID-reuse handling were settled in messages #152-#154.

Other privilege points look settled or follow existing practice. Message #158 revoked the reset functions from PUBLIC. Like pg_stat_all_tables and pg_stat_database, the views show all relations and databases without privilege checks. Per-object memory growth matches built-in pgstat. The safety of hook chaining with object_access_hook and with sepgsql cannot be checked without the code.
Patches 0001 to 0004 look like a reasonable first step on their own. These objections target the hook, the core sampling code and the contrib module.
Patches 0001-0004 add small columns that have no existing equivalent, so I raise nothing against them from this angle.

Patches 0001-0004 have demand shown in the thread. Sami asked for failsafe counts and vacuum time (messages #68, #75), and the delay and index time columns extend existing columns. The objections above concern only the hook and extension in 0005-0008.
